lines.text: Microsoft just walked away from an AI data centre, because there's not enough electricity for it.
It's Nscale's planned data centre in Loughton, Essex, near London. Microsoft was set to be its anchor customer.
The local grid operator, UK Power Networks, reportedly said it couldn't supply enough power until the early to mid 2030s.
The site was planned at 50 megawatts, with room to grow to 90.
Microsoft calls it a single-site decision. Nscale says the partnership is intact, with projects in Norway, Portugal and the US.
And it's a wider problem. Reuters says grid connection queues have delayed some data centre projects by as long as 13 years.
Why it matters: the AI race isn't just about chips anymore. It's about power, and in some places, the grid can't keep up.
